description: I am a high school student from Ethiopia interested in space science, satellite technology, Earth observation, and programming. Through the Ethiopian Space Science Society's SST26 training, I gained experience in GPS data analysis, research, teamwork, and technical presentations. I am looking to collaborate with curious and committed people interested in space science, coding, data analysis, design, writing and problem-solving.
summary:
For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I developed Project Dustbound Stories, an interactive digital storybook and mission journal that directly addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Instead of letting historic retired missions fade into dry telemetry archives, our project gives a true voice to NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B). Written from a compelling first-person perspective, it guides readers through Opportunity's incredible 15-year, 45.16-kilometer journey across the Martian landscape—from its 2004 landing at Eagle Crater all the way to its final days silenced by the 2018 global dust storm.   
This project is deeply important because it bridges the gap between complex planetary science and everyday readers, making space history engaging and emotionally resonant for students, educators, and space fans worldwide. By combining authentic NASA open data, sol logs, and official JPL surface imagery with creative narrative storytelling, we ensure that humanity's historic explorers are never forgotten.
details: ‎So for Project Dustbound Stories, here is the breakdown of what my project is all about: ‎ ‎What it does / How it works: I built an interactive digital storybook and mission journal that tells the 15-year journey of NASA's Opportunity rover on Mars from its own first-person perspective. It’s split into four main chapters—starting from its landing at Eagle Crater in 2004, uncovering ancient water, trekking across craters, and finally facing the 2018 global dust storm. It combines a narrative story format with real NASA logs, sol counts, and official surface photos. ‎ ‎Benefits: It takes dry, complicated scientific data and turns it into an emotional, gripping adventure story that's actually fun to read. ‎ ‎Intended Impact: I want to spark curiosity and inspire students, teachers, and anyone interested in space exploration by showing the true grit and engineering behind historic missions, while making sure retired explorers like Opportunity aren't forgotten. ‎ ‎Tools & Software Used: I used Google Docs and Google Slides to write, format, and host everything publicly, along with official NASA open data archives, the NASA Photojournal, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter orbital maps. ‎ ‎Why it's creative: Instead of just dropping a boring report full of bullet points and dry facts, we framed the whole project as a personal mission log written directly from the rover's point of view ("My journey began with a bounce..."). ‎ ‎What My team considered: I made sure to directly answer the Space Apps Challenge prompt ("Abandoned but not Forgotten"), kept our pitch deck strictly under the 7-slide limit, made sure all links are fully public and easy to open, and backed every single milestone up with authentic NASA open data.
